item.title: Daily Drill — decode one instruction
item.description:
Decode this byte sequence into its full assembly instruction (mnemonic + operands), Windows x86-64:
8B 04 8D 00 10 00 00
Break down the opcode, the ModRM byte, and the SIB byte. Pay special attention to what base=101 means in the SIB byte when mod=00 -- it isn't a normal base register.
---
Answer:
mov eax, [rcx*4 + 0x1000]
Explanation: 1. 8B is MOV r32, r/m32. ModRM 04 = mod=00, reg=000 (eax), rm=100 -- rm=100 means "no direct register, read a SIB byte next." 2. SIB 8D = scale=10b (x4), index=001b (rcx), base=101b. With mod=00 and base=101, this is the special no-base-register case: instead of using a base register, the encoding switches to a bare disp32 (added to the scaled index), so there's no [base + ...] term at all. 3. The trailing 4 bytes 00 10 00 00 (little-endian) give disp32 = 0x1000. Effective address = rcx*4 + 0x1000, loaded into eax.
